tool_calls.arguments:
{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "qPCR_plate_setup_6samples_triplicate", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tips = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 1)
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 2)
    master_mix_tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_2ml_snapcap", 4)
    temp_mod = protocol.load_module("temperature module gen2", 3)
    strip_tubes = temp_mod.load_labware("opentrons_96_aluminumblock_generic_pcr_strip_200ul")
    p300 = protocol.load_instrument("p300_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips])

    # Define liquids
    master_mix_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="master mix",
        description="SYBR master mix with primers",
        display_color="#FF0000"
    )
    sample1_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 1",
        description="cDNA sample 1",
        display_color="#00FF00"
    )
    sample2_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 2",
        description="cDNA sample 2",
        display_color="#0000FF"
    )
    sample3_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 3",
        description="cDNA sample 3",
        display_color="#FFFF00"
    )
    sample4_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 4",
        description="cDNA sample 4",
        display_color="#FF00FF"
    )
    sample5_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 5",
        description="cDNA sample 5",
        display_color="#00FFFF"
    )
    sample6_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 6",
        description="cDNA sample 6",
        display_color="#808080"
    )

    # Load liquids into source wells
    master_mix_tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=master_mix_liquid, volume=200)
    strip_tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=sample1_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A2"].load_liquid(liquid=sample2_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A3"].load_liquid(liquid=sample3_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A4"].load_liquid(liquid=sample4_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A5"].load_liquid(liquid=sample5_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A6"].load_liquid(liquid=sample6_liquid, volume=10)

    # Perform transfers
    p300.pick_up_tip()
    for i, well in enumerate(plate.wells()[:18]):
        sample_idx = i // 3  # 0-5
        # Aspirate 8 ul master mix
        p300.aspirate(8, master_mix_tubes["A1"])
        # Dispense 8 ul into well
        p300.dispense(8, well)
        # Aspirate 2 ul sample
        sample_source = strip_tubes["A" + str(sample_idx + 1)]
        p300.aspirate(2, sample_source)
        # Dispense 2 ul into well
        p300.dispense(2, well)
    p300.drop_tip()"}

tool_calls.arguments:
{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "qPCR_plate_setup_6samples_triplicate", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tips = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_20ul", 1)
    p20 = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips])
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 2)
    master_mix_tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_2ml_snapcap", 4)
    temp_mod = protocol.load_module("temperature module gen2", 3)
    strip_tubes = temp_mod.load_labware("opentrons_96_aluminumblock_generic_pcr_strip_200ul")
    # Set temperature to 4°C to preserve cDNA samples
    temp_mod.set_temperature(4)

    # Define liquids
    master_mix_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="master mix",
        description="SYBR master mix with primers",
        display_color="#FF0000"
    )
    sample1_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 1",
        description="cDNA sample 1",
        display_color="#00FF00"
    )
    sample2_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 2",
        description="cDNA sample 2",
        display_color="#0000FF"
    )
    sample3_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 3",
        description="cDNA sample 3",
        display_color="#FFFF00"
    )
    sample4_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 4",
        description="cDNA sample 4",
        display_color="#FF00FF"
    )
    sample5_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 5",
        description="cDNA sample 5",
        display_color="#00FFFF"
    )
    sample6_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 6",
        description="cDNA sample 6",
        display_color="#808080"
    )

    # Load liquids into source wells with realistic starting volumes
    master_mix_tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=master_mix_liquid, volume=200)
    strip_tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=sample1_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A2"].load_liquid(liquid=sample2_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A3"].load_liquid(liquid=sample3_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A4"].load_liquid(liquid=sample4_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A5"].load_liquid(liquid=sample5_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A6"].load_liquid(liquid=sample6_liquid, volume=10)

    # Perform transfers for 18 wells (6 samples x 3 replicates)
    for i, well in enumerate(plate.wells()[:18]):
        sample_idx = i // 3  # 0-5, each sample used for 3 consecutive wells
        # Aspirate 8 ul master mix and dispense into well
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        p20.aspirate(8, master_mix_tubes["A1"])
        p20.dispense(8, well)
        p20.drop_tip()
        # Aspirate 2 ul sample and dispense into same well
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        sample_source = strip_tubes["A" + str(sample_idx + 1)]
        p20.aspirate(2, sample_source)
        p20.dispense(2, well)
        p20.drop_tip()
    
    # Deactivate temperature module after protocol completion
    temp_mod.deactivate()"}

protocol.py: 2 biology problems (2 notes).

1. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 18 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 68:  p20.dispense(8, well)
   At line 68 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 2), and 18 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2
   and 10 more in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 8 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [2c950f3a8fd3]

2. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 18 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4
and 2 more went in (20% of the well)
   line 74:  p20.dispense(2, well)
   At line 74 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 2 more to wells A1,
   A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 2, which already held master mix (this
   line did it 18 times). The addition was 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be,
   mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 2 after line 74:
   `mix_after=(5, 8)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 8, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [b076a1a7dc9c]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "qPCR_plate_setup_6samples_triplicate", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tips = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_20ul", 1)
    p20 = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips])
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 2)
    master_mix_tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_2ml_snapcap", 4)
    temp_mod = protocol.load_module("temperature module gen2", 3)
    strip_tubes = temp_mod.load_labware("opentrons_96_aluminumblock_generic_pcr_strip_200ul")
    # Set temperature to 4°C to preserve cDNA samples
    temp_mod.set_temperature(4)

    # Define liquids
    master_mix_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="master mix",
        description="SYBR master mix with primers",
        display_color="#FF0000"
    )
    water_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="water",
        description="nuclease-free water",
        display_color="#000000"
    )
    sample1_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 1",
        description="cDNA sample 1",
        display_color="#00FF00"
    )
    sample2_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 2",
        description="cDNA sample 2",
        display_color="#0000FF"
    )
    sample3_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 3",
        description="cDNA sample 3",
        display_color="#FFFF00"
    )
    sample4_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 4",
        description="cDNA sample 4",
        display_color="#FF00FF"
    )
    sample5_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 5",
        description="cDNA sample 5",
        display_color="#00FFFF"
    )
    sample6_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 6",
        description="cDNA sample 6",
        display_color="#808080"
    )

    # Load liquids into source wells with realistic starting volumes
    master_mix_tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=master_mix_liquid, volume=200)
    master_mix_tubes["A2"].load_liquid(liquid=water_liquid, volume=20)
    strip_tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=sample1_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A2"].load_liquid(liquid=sample2_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A3"].load_liquid(liquid=sample3_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A4"].load_liquid(liquid=sample4_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A5"].load_liquid(liquid=sample5_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A6"].load_liquid(liquid=sample6_liquid, volume=10)

    # Perform transfers for 18 reaction wells (6 samples × 3 replicates)
    for i, well in enumerate(plate.wells()[:18]):
        sample_idx = i // 3  # 0‑5, each sample used for 3 consecutive wells
        # --- Add master mix (8 µL) ---
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        p20.aspirate(8, master_mix_tubes["A1"])
        p20.dispense(8, well)
        # --- Add sample (2 µL) or water for no‑template control ---
        if i == 18:  # after the 18 reaction wells, add a no‑template control well
            # Use well H12 as the NTC location
            ntc_well = plate["H12"]
            p20.dispense(8, ntc_well)  # 8 µL master mix already added above
            p20.aspirate(2, master_mix_tubes["A2"])  # aspirate water
            p20.dispense(2, ntc_well)  # add 2 µL water
            p20.drop_tip()
            continue
        # Normal transfer for reaction wells
        sample_source = strip_tubes["A" + str(sample_idx + 1)]
        p20.aspirate(2, sample_source)
        p20.dispense(2, well)
        # Mix the well (5 cycles, 8 µL total, ~80 % of well volume)
        p20.mix(5, 8, well)
        p20.drop_tip()
    
    # Deactivate temperature module after protocol completion
    temp_mod.deactivate()"}

protocol.py: 2 biology problems (1 warning, 1 note).

1. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 6 stocks
   line 86:  p20.aspirate(2, sample_source)
   At line 86 the tip went into sample 1 (well A1 in slot 3), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 3),
   sample 3 (well A3 in slot 3), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 3) and 2 more while it still
   carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step (this line did it 6 times). A
   tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so
   these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol drew from them
   again afterwards, but only into wells that were given that material on purpose anyway, so
   this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 86 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling

tool_calls.arguments:
{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {"protocolName": "qPCR_plate_setup_6samples_triplicate", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tips = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_20ul", 1)
    p20 = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips])
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 2)
    master_mix_tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_2ml_snapcap", 4)
    water_tube = master_mix_tubes["A2"]  # water source
    temp_mod = protocol.load_module("temperature module gen2", 3)
    strip_tubes = temp_mod.load_labware("opentrons_96_aluminumblock_generic_pcr_strip_200ul")
    # Set temperature to 4°C to preserve cDNA samples
    temp_mod.set_temperature(4)

    # Define liquids
    master_mix_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="master mix",
        description="SYBR master mix with primers",
        display_color="#FF0000"
    )
    water_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="water",
        description="nuclease-free water",
        display_color="#000000"
    )
    sample1_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 1",
        description="cDNA sample 1",
        display_color="#00FF00"
    )
    sample2_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 2",
        description="cDNA sample 2",
        display_color="#0000FF"
    )
    sample3_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 3",
        description="cDNA sample 3",
        display_color="#FFFF00"
    )
    sample4_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 4",
        description="cDNA sample 4",
        display_color="#FF00FF"
    )
    sample5_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 5",
        description="cDNA sample 5",
        display_color="#00FFFF"
    )
    sample6_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="sample 6",
        description="cDNA sample 6",
        display_color="#808080"
    )

    # Load liquids into source wells with realistic starting volumes
    master_mix_tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=master_mix_liquid, volume=200)
    water_tube.load_liquid(liquid=water_liquid, volume=20)
    strip_tubes["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=sample1_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A2"].load_liquid(liquid=sample2_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A3"].load_liquid(liquid=sample3_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A4"].load_liquid(liquid=sample4_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A5"].load_liquid(liquid=sample5_liquid, volume=10)
    strip_tubes["A6"].load_liquid(liquid=sample6_liquid, volume=10)

    # Perform transfers for 18 reaction wells (6 samples × 3 replicates)
    for i, well in enumerate(plate.wells()[:18]):
        sample_idx = i // 3  # 0‑5, each sample used for 3 consecutive wells
        # --- Add master mix (8 µL) ---
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        p20.aspirate(8, master_mix_tubes["A1"])
        p20.dispense(8, well)
        p20.drop_tip()
        # --- Add sample (2 µL) ---
        sample_source = strip_tubes["A" + str(sample_idx + 1)]
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        p20.aspirate(2, sample_source)
        p20.dispense(2, well)
        # Mix the well (5 cycles, 8 µL total, ~80 % of well volume)
        p20.mix(5, 8, well)
        p20.drop_tip()
    
    # Add a no‑template control well (e.g., H12) with 8 µL master mix + 2 µL water
    p20.pick_up_tip()
    p20.aspirate(8, master_mix_tubes["A1"])
    p20.dispense(8, plate["H12"])
    p20.aspirate(2, water_tube)
    p20.dispense(2, plate["H12"])
    p20.mix(5, 8, plate["H12"])
    p20.drop_tip()
    
    # Deactivate temperature module after protocol completion
    temp_mod.deactivate()"}

protocol.py: 1 biology problem (1 warning).

1. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (tube A2 in slot 4)
   line 90:  p20.aspirate(2, water_tube)
   At line 90 the tip went into water (tube A2 in slot 4) while it still carried master mix
   (tube A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
   not belong there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so this run is not harmed,
   but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: tube A2 in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 90 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
